prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the child nearest the camera wearer, roughly 0.5–1.5 m away in the lower foreground, while the standing adult is about 2–4 m ahead and usually to the left; background vehicles, curb, and lights are roughly 8–20 m away. It makes the foreground–background separation and the child’s arm’s-reach proximity clearer than the dark RGB, including partial bodies cut off at the bottom or right edge. Across the five frames, the child remains very close but shifts from right foreground toward the centre and then right edge, while the adult shifts across the upper field and is increasingly cropped. The smooth brightness gradients give only approximate metric distances, merge some people with the ground, and become unreliable near silhouettes, frame boundaries, and the bright lower-right region.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map distinguishes two people in the first two frames, with the nearer child below and to the right of the farther adult, and separately marks distant vehicles high in the scene. The child is approximately 0.5–1.5 m from the camera wearer and within the wearer’s arm-reach zone, whereas the adult is roughly 2–4 m away; the people appear about 1–3 m apart, with the child in front of and below the adult in image space. It clarifies object boundaries and partial occlusions that are difficult to see in the dark RGB, including a small region labeled skateboard near the first-frame adult’s feet and vehicles roughly 8–20 m away. Reliability is poor after the second frame: a person-sized region is mislabeled bird, most of the fourth frame is mislabeled bed, one car label is corrupted, and several visible people or body parts are missed or cut off, so later motion and facing direction cannot be trusted from this map alone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map recovers a partial skeleton for the left-side adult in frame 1 and a sparse, mostly vertical body trace for the adult in frame 2, placing both several metres ahead of the camera wearer and above the nearer child in image space. In frame 1 the detected torso and limbs suggest the adult is angled roughly side-on rather than squarely facing the camera, but head and eye orientation are too incomplete to establish whether the person looks toward the wearer. The skeleton makes limb arrangement and approximate reach around the adult clearer than the dark RGB, but it does not reliably detect the nearby child, hands, or any person in frames 3–5. Consequently, distances between joints, arm’s-reach relationships, occlusions, and changes such as turning or approach are largely unsupported; the isolated points and missing limbs indicate severe detection failure.
